channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Druze town cancels festival over fears of clashes and violence
item.description: Beit Jann's Yalla Ba'Galil festival, featuring Jewish and Druze artists, was canceled over fears of clashes, with reports saying Eden Ben-Zaken's planned performance sparked the dispute.

item.title: Promised reserved slot, then backtracked: Ex-hostage's mother slams Yair Golan
item.description: Einav Zangauker claims that during a meeting with Yair Golan in February, she was offered a reserved spot near the top of the Democrats’ Knesset slate and that the agreement was subsequently reaffirmed.

item.description: Suspect impersonated rival to threaten Ben-Gvir and MK Sukkot

item.title: 20 buildings collapse, at least 2 dead, in Colombia earthquake
item.description: At least two people have died and 20 buildings have collapsed in a powerful earthquake in the country of Colombia. Many people remain trapped under the debris.

item.title: 20 years after his death, Roi Klein's son follows in his father's footsteps
item.description: Twenty years after Major Roi Klein fell in Bint Jbeil, his eldest son Gilad enlisted in his father's Golani 51st Battalion alongside his brother.

item.title: Netanyahu launches national AI program: ‘Israel will be a global power’
item.description: In announcing AI program, PM Netanyahu says: “The future is not waiting for us; we are creating it."

item.title: 'Blood-boiling': Historic Irgun outpost in Safed vandalized
item.description: Safed historian Yaakov Schenkman discovered an Irgun heritage site vandalized, with its Israeli flag torn down, gate ripped out and trash strewn inside.

item.title: Board of Peace: Israel already implementing rejected Gaza plan
item.description: Senior officials behind US President Donald Trump's Gaza initiative say Israel's actions on the ground align with the 15-point proposal, despite Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's public rejection of it.

item.title: John Fetterman: 'Abdul El-Sayed has little-man syndrome energy'
item.description: Pro-Israel Democratic Senator responds to radical Michigan Senate nominee who called to put his head 'on a pike.'

item.title: Europe's Odyssey
item.description: Both Turkey and Qatar are strong supporters of the Muslim Brotherhood and collaborate to finance the construction of mosques in Europe.

item.title: Protecting Torah life in the digital age
item.description: We must protect our communities from online messages intended to weaken faith, normalize transgression, and influence others-particularly the young and vulnerable-to reject the sacred foundations of Jewish life.

item.title: Record number of illegal Palestinian structures demolished in Judea and Samaria
item.description: New Civil Administration data show record 536 illegal Arab structures demolished in just six months, as Israel steps up enforcement in Area C.

item.title: Massive brush fire races toward Gush Etzion farm
item.description: Strong winds driving fast-moving wildfire toward farm in Gush Etzion, firefighting aircraft and ground crews battle to halt advance.

item.title: Golani combat soldier dies by suicide in New York
item.description: William Shakin, a volunteer in the Golani Brigade who fought in Gaza, took his own life in New York after his mental health deteriorated. His parents seek to have him buried in the military cemetery on Mount Herzl.

item.title: Justice shouldn't take 25 years
item.description: 25 years ago, my daughter was killed in the Sbarro bombing. Why is her killer still free?

item.title: Be’eri survivor: ‘Hamas will not disarm - Israel must show determination’
item.description: Avida Bachar, who lost his wife and son on October 7, says Israel must reject any deal that leaves Hamas in control of Gaza and show determination to prevent another massacre.

item.title: NIS 5 million fraud: Electricity bills allegedly erased for cash
item.description: Customers paid a fraction of their electricity debts to have them illegally wiped from Israel Electric Corporation records, police say.

item.title: Sanzer Rebbe: Most Israelis do not hate Torah learners
item.description: Sanzer Rebbe meet young haredi recently freed from military prison, praises his steadfastness, insisting 'most Jews in Israel' do not hate Torah students.

item.title: Health Ministry official: 'BBC dropped interview after I questioned its reporting'
item.description: Prof. Mitch Schwaber says he asked a senior BBC correspondent how the network would ensure accuracy in a report on Gaza's health situation after citing six examples of what he described as errors and journalistic negligence.

item.title: Iran: Strait of Hormuz won't reopen until US pays price
item.description: Tehran says Washington must end its military pressure and compensate Iran before the crucial shipping lane can be considered open again.

item.title: Opposing Defense Min.: Maj.Gen. Avi Bluth expels Tal Yinon Dardik from Samaria
item.description: Central Command chief Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth decided, contrary to the Defense Minister’s request, to renew the administrative detention order against Tal Yinon Dardik, who is suspected of assaulting a Palestinian.

item.title: Israel demands answers on Ron Arad, missing Jews in Lebanon talks
item.description: Lebanese media say Israel used latest round of negotiations to press for answers on Ron Arad and other Jews missing since Lebanon's civil war.

item.title: Israel Railways expands ETCS pilot to the north
item.description:
Israel Railways has begun conducting passenger-free test runs on the Karmiel-Ahihud line using the ETCS control and signaling system, following the launch of the pilot in the Jerusalem area, Modi'in, and along the Ayalon corridor.
According to Israel Railways, the system is designed to enable an increase in train frequency using the existing rail infrastructure, while improving safety and the management of train traffic.

item.title: Study warns: Israel's eastern border could become 'next October 7'
item.description: A new study paints a troubling picture of the Jordanian border, urging Israel to strengthen ties with Jordan, accelerate construction of border and reinforce Jordan Valley communities.

item.title: Former Beit Shemesh mayor joins Erdan-Edelstein party
item.description: Aliza Bloch officially joins new political party founded by former ministers Gilad Erdan and Yuli Edelstein, after reportedly turning down reserved spot on Likud list.

item.title: Exclusive: Jurisdiction of Givat Harel officially approved
item.description: The jurisdiction of Givat Harel (Carmei Oz) over declared state lands has been officially approved, with Kida and Esh Kodesh receiving official recognition. Israel Ganz: 'A major step toward growth in Binyamin.'

item.title: No relief yet: Heat wave to continue through the week
item.description: Scorching conditions continue across Israel, with Jordan Valley expected to reach 44°C as forecasters warn of heavy to extreme heat stress.

item.title: What Status Quo? The real implications of the 'Mecca Joint Defense Agreement'
item.description: Deterrence replaces normalization: Riyadh has found a way to build real security architecture - with a NATO military power and with the only nuclear state in the Muslim world - without having to declare that it is actually abandoning Washington's normalization track.

item.title: Israeli sovereignty NOW
